newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Foreign oil stocks rise in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Foreign oil stocks rise in New York.

text.p: Foreign oil companies largely rose on Friday to highlight quiet trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said ADRs were boosted with the rest of the markets by the government's release of weaker-than-expected February economic data. The figures eased fears of an interest rate hike.
"Things are bouncing back on relief that Wall Street is recovering from yesterday's losses," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities.
Oil stocks were boosted in part by a rise in crude oil prices. Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was up three to 175-7/8, helped by presentations to analysts this week in London and New York.
Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc rose one to 103-1/4, Britain's LASMO Plc was up 7/8 to 12-1/4 and Spain's Repsol SA rose 5/8 to 41-1/4.
Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc rose one to 32 after the company said it was replacing the head of its Burger King Corp fast-food restaurant unit.
China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd rose 1-3/4 to a record 29-3/4 in follow-through from overnight buying in Hong Kong.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras rose 1-3/4 to 107.
Advancers led decliners by 251 to 182 among 806 ADRs. ADRs showed an overall rise of 0.39 percent and volume was 18.2 million shares in late morning.
